items.q: Your rectangle sketch shows blue lines. After adding horizontal and vertical relations and two dimensions, all lines turn black. What does black mean?
options: The sketch is locked from editing
items.explain: Black means every entity is fixed by relations and dimensions; blue entities can still be dragged, so the geometry is not yet pinned down.

items.q: A sketch of a 25 mm x 100 mm rectangle is revolved 360 degrees about its 100 mm edge. What solid results?
items.explain: The 25 mm side becomes the radius when spun about the 100 mm axis, so the diameter is 50 mm and the length is 100 mm.

items.q: The drawing calls for R3 on all outer edges of a block. Which feature do you apply?
items.explain: R3 means a 3 mm radius round on the edge, which is a fillet; a chamfer would be a flat bevel.

items.q: After a Concentric mate, a shaft can still slide along the hole and rotate. You want to stop the sliding but keep the rotation. Which mate do you add?
options: Parallel mate between the two axes
Tangent mate between the cylindrical faces
Coincident mate between the shaft shoulder face and housing face
items.explain: A coincident mate between two flat faces removes the axial translation while leaving rotation about the axis free.

items.q: A part inserted into an assembly has 6 degrees of freedom. After one Concentric mate between two cylindrical faces, how many are left?
items.explain: Concentric locks two translations and two rotations, leaving translation along the axis and rotation about it.

items.q: A boss extrude uses the Mid Plane end condition with depth 40 mm. How far does the solid grow on each side of the sketch plane?
items.explain: Mid Plane splits the total depth equally about the sketch plane, so 40 mm total is 20 mm each way.

items.q: A hole on a drawing carries the feature control frame [Position] dia 0.2 | A | B. What does it require?
options: The hole is concentric to datum A within 0.2 mm
The hole diameter can vary by 0.2 mm
The hole axis lies inside a 0.2 mm diameter zone located from datums A and B
The hole surface is flat within 0.2 mm
items.explain: Position tolerance controls where the axis is, not the size; the diameter symbol makes the tolerance zone a cylinder of 0.2 mm.

items.q: A shaft is dimensioned dia 20 h7. Which size range is acceptable?
items.explain: An h tolerance always has its upper limit at the nominal size, and IT7 for 18 to 30 mm is 21 microns below it.

items.q: A tiny R0.5 groove is too small to dimension clearly on the main view of a drawing. Which view do you add?
options: A detail view at a larger scale
items.explain: A detail view enlarges a circled area of an existing view so small features can be dimensioned.

items.q: An assembly contains 4 bolts inserted as 4 instances of the same part file. How does the bill of materials show them?
options: Four rows, one for each bolt
One row for the bolt with QTY 4
items.explain: The BOM groups identical components by part and counts the instances, so the same file appears once with quantity 4.

items.q: You dimension a sketch line to 50 mm, then try to add a second dimension of 60 mm to the same line. What happens?
options: The sketch becomes over-defined and the tool offers to make it a driven (reference) dimension
The first dimension is deleted automatically
items.explain: Two driving dimensions on one length conflict; the tool flags over-definition and lets the new one be reference-only.
